stories.headline: ‘We don’t condone cheating’: IIT Bombay students call for reforms after Sahil’s death
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Student representatives at IIT Bombay have issued an official statement following the death of student Sahil Wakode, saying they do not condone cheating or any form of academic misconduct, while calling for reforms to address systemic concerns within the institute.
“We do not stand for or condone cheating or any form of academic misconduct. At the same time, the loss of our fellow student, Sahil, is a deeply tragic event that has compelled us to reflect on the systems and processes within our Institute,” the representatives said.
They said the protest launched by students was not intended to justify academic misconduct, but was a collective effort to raise concerns over issues that had existed within the institute for some time and seek “meaningful and strong institutional reforms” to prevent similar circumstances in the future.
The representatives also welcomed the open house held with the institute's Director and other members of the administration on Sunday, saying it gave students an opportunity to directly raise their concerns and questions.
Back fair probe into Professor Doolla
On Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, the students clarified that they had never presumed his guilt or sought to prejudge the ongoing investigation.
“We stand with Professor Doolla as a member of our faculty community and believe that the investigation must be allowed to proceed fairly and impartially,” they said.
The students said their demand was for Doolla to be relieved of his administrative responsibilities as Dean of Administrative Affairs while the investigation is underway. They described this as a precautionary measure intended to ensure that the probe remains independent and cannot be influenced in any manner.

“The findings and appropriate action should follow from the established investigative process,” the representatives said.
Oppose external political influence
The student representatives said concerns arising from Sahil’s death should remain student-led and be addressed within the institute.
“The loss of Sahil should not become a platform for external political interests, organisations, or narratives to shape the concerns of the IIT Bombay student community,” they said.
They added that the demands had emerged from students’ experiences and concerns on campus, and that the reform process should remain rooted in the student community and the institute.

stories.headline: After Meta, Google to report child abuse material directly to India
stories.deck: Google to report child sexual abuse material directly to Indian authorities
stories.bodyText: New Delhi: Google has agreed to report content flagged as child sexual abuse material (CSAM) directly to Indian authorities, the company said on Monday..A Google spokesperson stated: “Google is deeply committed to fighting CSAM online and preventing its platforms from being used to create, store or distribute such material. We invest significantly to detect, deter, remove and report child sexual abuse material. As part of our ongoing discussions with the Government of India, we have respectfully proposed to operationalise the provision of relevant information to the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) in cases related to child sexual abuse material.”.The move follows a similar decision by Meta last week. Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, has established a direct reporting pipeline to the cybercrime portal managed by the I4C..Until now, US-based platforms including Google and Meta primarily routed such cases through the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) in the United States..Google says its AI hacked three companies in testing breakout.Indian officials had pressed tech firms in recent weeks to report CSAM cases involving India directly to domestic agencies. They argued that routing reports through NCMEC created delays that could prove critical when a child is in active danger, according to government sources..The government has described the online safety of children as a "non-negotiable" principle for platforms operating in India..India represents the largest user market for both YouTube and Meta’s platforms. Meta’s decision came amid heightened friction with the Central government, including an apology last month by CEO Mark Zuckerberg over the spread of CSAM on its services.

stories.headline: 'Historic occasion': Jaishankar describes first V4+India Foreign Ministers meeting
stories.deck: The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia that aims at advancing co-operation in military, economic, cultural and energy affairs
stories.bodyText:
India and the four-member Visegrad group of Central European countries on Monday (September 21, 2026) agreed to step up political, economic and defence cooperation at their first Foreign Ministers' meeting, which External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar described as a “new historic occasion”.
The Visegrad Group (V4) is a cultural and political alliance of the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia that aims to advance cooperation in military, economic, cultural, and energy affairs.
The first meeting between the Foreign Ministers of the Visegrad Group and India was held on Monday (September 21, 2026), on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
Mr Jaishankar met with Poland's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Radek Sikorski; Hungary's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Anita Orban; Slovakia's Minister of Foreign and European Affairs, Juraj Blanar; and the Czech Minister of Foreign Affairs, Petr Macinka.
"It was, in a sense, a new historic occasion,” Mr. Jaishankar said in remarks after the meeting.
"It was a very, very productive meeting. What we agreed was that since India's relationship with the European Union itself is deepening, with the V4 we would take some special initiatives to create an annual business forum,” he said, adding that there was “consensus" that the Foreign Ministers of the five nations in the group would meet annually.
“We would also explore technology and innovation whether we could be doing more. We have a very strong history with all the V4 countries in defence. We want to refresh and take forward that record and that cooperation,” Mr. Jaishankar said.
The group also discussed issues including space, connectivity, and people-to-people mobility.
Mr. Jaishankar said the meeting was “very worthwhile” and “very productive”, with discussions focusing on cooperation as well as major global crises, including the Ukraine conflict and developments in the Gulf.
“It was really a very, very worthwhile, very productive meeting. I'm very pleased about it,” he said in remarks to reporters after the meeting.
In a post on X, Mr. Jaishankar said the first meeting in the V4+India format agreed to closer political cooperation, including annual meetings of foreign ministers, and deeper economic cooperation, including the Annual Business Forum.
The countries also agreed to strengthen technology, innovation, research and education partnerships; reinvigorate defence cooperation; further develop cultural cooperation and people-to-people relations and work together to support multilateralism, he said.
Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has “very good” relations with the V4 countries.
"These are countries with a very strong, very distinctive capability. These are industrial economies, economies with great innovation and technology talent, and I think how the V4 come together is for them to decide. But we certainly welcome the opportunity to work with the V4 together,” he told reporters.

stories.headline: India-New Zealand FTA to kick in Oct 20, opening a zero-tariff export window
stories.deck: India, New Zealand FTA to come into force from October 20
stories.bodyText: New Delhi: Free trade agreement between India and New Zealand, which was signed in April this year, will come into effect from October 20, paving the way for duty-free access for Indian goods in New Zealand markets..“We have chosen the auspicious day Vijay Dashmi for the entry into force of the India-New Zealand FTA,” Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal told reporters on Monday..New Zealand’s Minister for Trade and Investment Todd McClay held a virtual conference with Goyal to finalise the date for implementation of the deal, which was signed on April 27..Goyal said every single tariff line covering 100% of India's exports to New Zealand would become duty-free from the first day of the implementation of the deal..At present, New Zealand’s peak tariffs on Indian products stand at 10%. Labour intensive sectors like textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods and processed foods are likely to gain the most from the deal..Bilateral merchandise trade between India and New Zealand stood at $1.1 billion in 2025-26. According to the minister, the deal is expected to give a decisive push to two-way trade..Investment facilitation is another important feature of the deal. As part of the deal New Zealand has committed to facilitate $20 billion investment in India..Explained | From luxury cars and Scotch whisky to medical equipment: Here's what gets cheaper as India-UK FTA comes into effect.“This investment by New Zealand will benefit Indian agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and start-ups,” the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said..On the other hand India has offered to reduce tariffs and provide greater market access to New Zealand through a combination of “immediate and phased tariff liberalisation and tariff rate quotas.”.Around 30% of tariff lines will enjoy immediate duty-free access, covering products such as wood, wool, sheep meat, leather products-raw hides etc. A further 35.6% of tariff lines will see progressive tariff elimination over periods ranging from 3 to 10 years, including petroleum oils, malt extracts, vegetable oils, peptones, selected electrical and mechanical machinery..“A calibrated market access has been structured for New Zealand’s apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey through Tariff Rate Quotas with Minimum Import Price and seasonal import windows, alongside safeguards to protect domestic farmers,” the commerce ministry said..The FTA with New Zealand offers opportunities for engineering goods exporters to diversify their product line-up. With the trade agreement coming into force next month, we can certainly target the doubling of engineering exports in the next five years to $280-300 million, said Pankaj Chadha, Chairman, Engineering Export Promotion Council (EEPC) India.

briefs.headline: Asian Games 2026 | With gold in sight, India settle for silver again
briefs.deck: Asian Games: With gold in sight, India settle for silver again
briefs.bodyText: Aichi (Japan): For a good part of the men’s 10m air rifle final, Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh B Patil were engaged in an intense battle with China’s Lihao Sheng at the shooting range in Aichi on Monday..All of 21, Sheng is ranked world No. 1, has two gold medals from the 2024 Paris Olympics and a silver from the 2021 Tokyo Games, and entered the 20th Asian Games as the defending champion in the event..Himanshu, 20, and Rudrankksh, 22, have impressive profiles of their own and were well aware of the tall task ahead. Ultimately, the two Indians, focused primarily on themselves rather than their rivals, took turns leading the field before relentlessly chasing Sheng. But an unperturbed Sheng held his nerve to walk away with gold and Games and Asian records with a score of 254.2 points..Once again, a top-of-the-podium finish was within sight for the Indians. In the end, they had to settle for the other two medals on offer instead. On the second day of the shooting competition, slow starter Himanshu finished strongly to win silver with 252.4 points, while early leader Rudrankksh lost momentum to take bronze with 230.9..Earlier, the combined qualification efforts of the two youngsters and teenager Parth Mane helped India finish second in the team event. Any guesses who won team gold? The Chinese, of course. Sheng, along with Changhong Zhang and Sihan Ma, shattered China’s previous world record of 1898.4 points to set a new mark of 1899.0..Qualifying third, Rudrankksh, a former world No. 1, moved to the top spot and stayed there until the 15th shot of the 24-shot elimination format in the individual final. By then, Dhillon, who had initially lingered in the middle of the field, had climbed to second courtesy of some perfect 10.9s. Sheng remained a mere 0.1 point behind in third..The script of the final completely flipped from shot 16. Sheng’s 10.7 catapulted him into pole position, while lower 10 scores from the Indian duo suddenly pushed them back into the role of chasers..It was after shot 18 that the Indians realised gold was beginning to slip out of reach. Dhillon’s 9.8 made the packed gallery erupt in a collective gasp. The birthday boy’s fumble pushed him down to third, with Rudrankksh still just 0.5 points behind leader Sheng..But Sheng isn't the one to surrender any sort of lead. Parallally, Himanshu regrouped and, over the final six shots, outshot a tiring Rudrankksh to finish as the better-placed of the two Indians..“Colour of the medal can change, but all I knew was I didn’t want to give up until the end,” said Himanshu in the post-event interaction..Asked whether a prolific shooter like Sheng intimidated him during the final of his maiden Asian Games, Himanshu said: “When we are all in a changing room, we see them and think they are legends in shooting. But at the firing point, like me, they too start from zero. We both have to start from zero. Then it’s the one who has the strength who wins. So, I was just focused on myself.”.The young brigade of 10m rifle shooters, with four silvers and a bronze from two days of competition, have set the right tone for the rest of their colleagues to reproduce and emulate.

briefs.headline: Many other Shivanis: ‘Tailgated, provoked to race, shown the middle finger’ – a day in the life of women riding bikes
briefs.bodyText:
Her injuries will heal, but riding a bike will not be the same again for Shivani Chauhan, who survived a road rage incident in Gurgaon last week in which a man in a car chased Shivani and knocked her off her moving bike on Golf Course Road. “I don't know when I'll start riding again, but whenever I do, I'll have that fear that this can happen again – that another car can come from behind and hit me,” she says.
It’s a fear women bike riders understand, and echo, because of what they describe as “unprovoked aggression” that comes their way on roads. Riders TOI spoke to described being chased, tailgated, obstructed, challenged to race and subjected to lewd gestures simply for being women on motorcycles.
'Danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads': Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick - Pune
Delhi-based rider Neharika Yadav said men have chased her from different angles to take photographs or start conversations, while Gurgaon rider Geetika Khurana recalled an incident of men blocking her way and revving alongside her to provoke a race. Male drivers revving their engines, driving dangerously close, honking incessantly – Mumbai-based motorcycle trainer and motivational speaker Shilpa Balakrishnan (51) describes this as a “routine” experience for woman on bikes.
 “Many have tried to corner me when I overtake. They behave this way simply because they see a woman riding,” she says.
‘Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem  to digest a woman  on two wheels’: Neharika Yadav, Delhi
The India Women Rider Safety and Mobility Report 2026, based on responses from 542 women riders, found that 57% had experienced harassment on the road.
For Shivani (27), who started riding only two years ago, the Sept 13 incident has forever changed the “therapeutic experience” of riding her Aprilia. “The incident keeps playing on my mind on a loop every now and then. It has affected me very badly, I think it will be a long time before I’m able to pick up the bike again,” says Shivani, who had kept her biker identity a secret on social media. As ‘Sia’, she felt freedom.
‘It feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road’ — Soundari Sindy, Chennai
Neharika, a dentist based in Delhi, and Pune-based fashion designer Maral Yazarloo-Pattrick (45) can relate. “I ride a bike because it gives me joy, not because I want to prove anything to anyone. In Delhi-NCR, we get cast into a stereotype. Even in 2026, there are men who can’t seem to digest a woman coming on two wheels. Since traffic here is dense, there are men like (Kalyan) Bainsla (who attacked Shivani) who will not give space to a woman rider. They will keep instigating you. I think they get some perverse joy out of it,” she says.
Yazarloo-Pattrick says danger is a tax women bikers pay on roads and freedom is the reason they keep paying it. “Such behaviour is an everyday reality. I’m shocked that anyone in India is surprised,” she says. Earlier this month, she was returning from Ladakh when she noticed a black SUV without a number plate following her. She switched on her GoPro but did not try to outrun it. Instead, she slowed down and pulled into a petrol pump. “If someone is chasing me and I cannot safely get away, I always head towards a crowded place.”
'While going from Gwalior to Hyderabad, a group of men followed me for 45 minutes': Atulya, Rajasthan
Suparna Sarkar (39), chief instructor at a motorcycle training academy in Gurgaon, tells TOI what made Shivani’s case different was that the aggression was caught on camera. “It’s just that she had a camera, so it led to widespread anger. Girls I teach biking to often share incidents where either people tried to race from behind or they were hit,” she says. Sarkar has experienced it herself. In 2023, she was riding near Mahipalpur in Delhi when a vehicle hit her. “There were no cameras in the area. I didn’t have a camera either,” she says.
Patriarchal conditioning has taught men that women must be watched,  judged and  corrected — Devika Mehta, Noida 
Soundari Sindy, a lawyer in her mid-30s based out of Chennai, says attitude towards women riding bikes is similar across the country. “It almost feels like we are hurting the male ego just by being on the road,” she tells TOI. A professional racer, Soundari commands a 150cc bike with her 5ft 1in frame. “Snide comments are common. There are strangers who have made fun of me, saying my feet would not touch the ground,” she says.
Sandhya Das, a 38-year-old IT professional who rides with Soundari, agrees that the sight of her on a bike is somehow “not palatable to some men”, whether she is in traditional attire or in biker gear with a jacket and gloves. “Men have tried to zip past me and tried to throw me off balance,” she says.
Just treat us like a normal rider — Riya Yadav, Gurgaon 
Chetana Naik (37) from Mumbai, who twice encountered a group of make bikers intimidating and overtaking her – in Kashmir recently and in Punjab earlier – adds, “For some men, being overtaken by a woman appears to be an insult that must be avenged. They begin intimidating us till their egos are satisfied,” she says.
Professional rider Anita Krishnan says even riding gear can be misread by some motorists as an invitation to race. “They start racing with you. It could be a car or even a bike. They will whizz past you at speed, trying to entice you into a race. This is very common,” she says. For long-distance riders, she points out, jackets, helmets and boots are protection from crashes, flying debris, rain, heat and cold, not racing gear.
Krishnan says she sometimes tucks her hair inside her jacket so motorists cannot immediately tell that she is a woman. “The gear also camouflages whether you are a woman. If your hair is out, only then people would know you are a woman. So, I would mostly hide my hair,” she says.
For 23-year-old Anainah Batiwala, camouflage goes further. The Mumbaikar does not feel comfortable riding in shorts and, after dark, goes out in baggy clothes. “I dress like a guy in baggy pants,” she says. “I wear my actual going-out clothes underneath.”
Atulya (23) remembers being scared for her life a couple of years ago while travelling from Gwalior to Hyderabad. A group of men followed her bike relentlessly for about 45 minutes on the highway. “I kept riding for about 10-15km even after I lost them. I was so scared that something would happen to me if I applied the brakes,” she says.
Atulya, who is originally from Kerala but grew up in Rajasthan, has been riding her bike all over India from the age of 18. While the incident rattled her, she decided to keep going.
Delhi-based biker Meenakshi says long group rides can become particularly vulnerable on the return journey because riders who set out together often disperse while heading home. “Often, we get calls from riders asking for help from passers-by, or they call us to say that two or three people are following them,” she says. Krishnan says women travelling alone or in smaller groups also become more selective about where they stop after dark and often share their live location with family members.
Organised riding groups have built formal safety systems around that vulnerability. Some assign a leader at the front, a tail rider to make sure nobody is left behind, and a marshal to keep both ends connected. “Men may have the liberty to stop anywhere, but women have to take extra precaution,” says Saify Ratlamwala, who runs riding groups in Navi Mumbai.
Devika Mehta, a media professional from Noida, narrates how a BMW came dangerously close to her bike on a curved road, nearly running her off.
“Remarks, lewd gestures, honking, and constant stares make our freedom rides really ugly. If they don’t hit you, they will come extremely close or follow to just mess with you,” the 40-year-old says, blaming this behaviour on “generations of patriarchal conditioning that has taught men that women must be watched, judged and corrected”. “Add weak impulse control, peer bravado, lax policing and near-zero consequences and harassment starts to feel normal, even entertaining, to them,” Devika says.
Geetika (25), a PR professional based in Gurgaon, said catcalling, teasing and obstructing the way are things most women riders have gone through in NCR. “The day I took my first ride, the experience was not pleasant. A group of boys obstructed my way and challenged me to race with them by coming close and revving their bikes. Since then, I’ve only taken my bike out early morning when I’m assured of encountering the least traffic.”
Sarkar says it’s “not all bad that women just can’t ride on Delhi-NCR roads”, but agreed there is a “section of people who create nuisance” and that can happen anytime. “It’s not only a women rider problem, but a women safety and road safety issue. When people are on the road, they should behave. When someone is driving a car, there is a base, there is support, it will not lose balance. But when you are on a two-wheeler, even the minutest touch will make you fall,” adds Sarkar.
Though less exposed than those on two-wheelers, women who drive cars say they have also encountered a “sense of entitlement” from strangers on the road, including cab drivers.
Pooja (38), who has been driving for 12 years in Delhi, says comments are common, not because she has done anything to provoke it but because it’s a woman at the wheel. “I keep getting told by strangers that the size of my car (a Scorpio) doesn’t ‘match’ mine.”
Rupali, an advertising professional from Noida, says she once deliberately slowed down to let a group of men overtake her in their car, just so she wouldn’t be harassed. This did not deter them. “They stopped and waited for me to pass, rolled down the windows and showed me their middle fingers,” the 35-year-old says. After they sped off, Rupali says, she drove at 30kmph so she wouldn’t encounter them again.
Yet the hostility has not stopped more women from taking up motorcycles. Meenakshi says the number of women she sees learning to ride has increased sharply. “Three years ago, if I trained 10 women in a month, the number would be 60-70 now,” she says. The profile, according to Krishnan, is changing too, with women in their 40s, 50s and even 60s increasingly taking up long-distance riding.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
Dnyanadaa Mhaskar is an example of that change. The Navi Mumbai schoolteacher began riding at 41, bought a motorcycle while still on a learner’s licence and, by her own account, barely knew how to work the clutch and gears. She later borrowed her grocer’s 100cc Hero for a ride to Pune and joined an all-women motorcycling group. Now 54, she says simply: “Riding is my solace and my bike is my soulmate.”
Riya Yadav, a Gurgaon-based professional biker who has been riding since she was a teenager, adds, “People need to realise that we are just riding a bike. We are not doing some rocket science. Just treat us like a normal rider.”
Most of these women say they have learnt to live with the unwanted attention on roads. “I think society at large has to change for us to see any meaningful change in men’s mindset towards a female driver. Till then, women need to take utmost precautions while riding. And be brave,” Shivani says.

briefs.headline: GST rate cuts have been offset by ‘galloping’ inflation: Congress
briefs.deck: The prices of several consumer goods had returned to nearly their pre-GST cut levels without any significant increase in consumption, the Congress spokesman claimed
briefs.bodyText:
The Congress said on Monday (September 21, 2026) that the impact of GST rate cuts on a range of commodities was being eroded by “galloping inflation”, with prices of several consumer products returning to pre-cut levels within a year.
Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh, sharing a media report on the issue, said the GST rationalisation announced in September 2025 had been “long overdue”, but its impact on consumption had been uneven.
“The GST rate cuts in September 2025 were proclaimed to be game changers. They had, of course, been long overdue — but to boast of them as magic wands was hyperbole. In fact, their impact on boosting consumption has been mixed at best. For instance, automobile sales benefited while apparel sales did not,” Mr. Ramesh said in a post on X.
“Now comes evidence that the effect of GST rate cuts on various commodities is being neutralised by ‘galloping inflation’,” he said.
The prices of several consumer goods had returned to nearly pre-GST cut levels within a year without any significant increase in consumption, Mr. Ramesh claimed.
He also linked the issue to the broader state of the economy, questioning the narrative around India’s growth based on headline GDP figures.
“Headline quarterly GDP numbers may give momentary elation to the ruling establishment overlooking their imperfections, but there are many faultlines in the India growth story that are simply not being acknowledged by the PM and his brigade of cheerleaders,” he said.
“Neither is consumption buoyant across income segments nor is private investment booming,” Mr. Ramesh said, adding that real wages were declining.

briefs.headline: Former V-P Hamid Ansari’s remarks exposed ‘Muslim League-Maoist character’ of Congress, says BJP
briefs.deck: At an event commemorating late constitutional expert A.G. Noorani, Hamid Ansari had referred to former PM’s view saying that ‘the real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism’, citing Noorani’s book The RSS: A Menace to India
briefs.bodyText:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday (September 21, 2026) claimed that former Vice-President Hamid Ansari “exposed” the “Muslim League-Maoist character” of the Congress party through his remarks about former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru’s views on “Hindu right-wing communalism”.
At an event commemorating late constitutional expert A.G. Noorani on Saturday (September 19), Mr. Ansari had referred to the former Prime Minister’s view saying that “the real danger to India was not communism, but Hindu right-wing communalism’, citing Noorani’s book The RSS: A Menace to India.
Addressing a press conference, BJP MP and national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said the former Vice-President quoted the book, according to which Mr. Nehru said that for him communism was not as great a threat as Hindu nationalism.
“For this, I would like to congratulate Hamid Ansari ji that he has done three extremely important things. Number one, he has thoroughly exposed that the Congress has now completely become a Maoist Muslim League Congress. Secondly, he deserves congratulations for quoting that, according to Nehru ji considered communism a threat. For the third point,..who brought up the reference to Nehru?” he said.
“We want to remind you that [Congress leader] Rahul Gandhi, while addressing the Press Club in Washington D.C., on June 2, 2023, said: ‘Muslim League is absolutely secular’...The Muslim League that was established by Jinnah is the same party with which you are running the government in Kerala today. It is a black chapter in the history of independent India that five Ministers in the Kerala government are from the Muslim League,” he said.
“If anyone claims that this Muslim League — meaning the Indian Union Muslim League formed in March 1949 — is not Jinnah’s Muslim League, they are telling an outright lie. This is because its founder, Mohammed Ismail, was the president of the Madras Presidency unit of Jinnah’s Muslim League,” said the BJP leader.

briefs.headline: US to reopen Cold War-era base, set up new military presence in Greenland: Report
briefs.bodyText:
The United States plans to reopen a former Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and establish a military presence at an eastern Greenland outpost currently used by Denmark's Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, according to report by Reuters.
The move is expected to be part of a new security agreement between the United States, Denmark and Greenland that the three sides are expected to sign on Tuesday on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The sites are Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland, where the US operated the Bluie West One military base until the 1950s, and Mestersvig on Greenland's east coast, which is currently used by the Sirius Dog Sled Patrol, a Danish special forces unit, two of the sources said.
The agreement is expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly in New York at 10:30 a.m. ET (1430 GMT) on Tuesday.
The text of the agreement has not been made public. The sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said its details had not been finalised and could change before the signing.
The governments of Denmark and Greenland did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The White House also did not immediately respond.
Deal follows Trump's pressure over Greenland
The agreement comes after months of pressure from US President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly said he wants the United States to control Greenland and has at times declined to rule out using military or economic force to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish territory.
Trump's threats, which intensified in January, triggered a diplomatic crisis within NATO and led Denmark and Greenland to negotiate with Washington in an effort to ease tensions.
Denmark has said the new agreement would place Arctic security within the framework of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization rather than leave responsibility solely with the United States and Denmark.
US military presence in Greenland
The United States maintained a much larger military presence in Greenland during the Cold War, operating 17 military installations and deploying more than 10,000 personnel there.
Today, only Pituffik Space Base remains as a US military installation in Greenland, with around 150 US military personnel.
The planned return to Narsarsuaq and presence at Mestersvig would expand the US military footprint on the strategically important Arctic island, although the precise scale and nature of the deployments were not immediately clear.
Greenland is a semi-autonomous territory of Denmark and occupies a strategically important position between North America and Europe. Its location also makes it important for monitoring activity in the Arctic and the North Atlantic.

briefs.headline: Amid Trump’s clash with CNN, Politico, MS NOW, White House launches ‘Trump TV’
briefs.bodyText:
The White House on Monday launched ‘TRUMP TV: The Essentials Station’, a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other content, as the Trump administration faces a legal challenge from CNN, MS NOW and Politico over their exclusion from the White House.
The White House said the new service would bring the administration's "biggest moments" together in one place, with content updated in real time. The stream was launched on the White House's YouTube channel at 7 pm ET on Monday.
The launch came hours after CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking to restore their access to the White House. The organisations argue that the administration's decision to revoke their journalists' credentials violates their First Amendment rights.
Trump had barred the three outlets from the White House after criticising their coverage. Their reporters were denied entry to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their press credentials confiscated, according to the organisations.
CNN was also removed from its scheduled television pool duties. ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC subsequently joined CNN in suspending their participation in the White House television pool after CNN was removed from a scheduled assignment.
The television pool normally provides shared video coverage of presidential events to broadcasters and other news organisations. With the pool disrupted, the White House's own video feed has become a more prominent source of footage from presidential events.
Trump on Monday sharply criticised the three organisations in a social media post after they sued his administration.
"As expected, Fake News CNN, Politico (Pay back the 8 Million Dollar contribution made by the U.S. Government to keep them afloat!), and MSNOW (formerly known as MSDNC!), have brought suit to gain access to the White House, and your President, ME! They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet. The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by “TRUMP.” In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown “sources,” shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World. It is called the Oval Office, and it should be treated with Decorum, Respect, and Dignity, not defiled by Third Rate Clowns, who purposefully distort, twist, and degrade with everything they write or publish. Virtually every story about me, or anything having to do with me, is negative, wrong and, in many cases, DANGEROUS for our Country! No matter how GREAT my Achievements, they trivialize and demean. The fact is, I won all seven Swing States, the Popular Vote, the Electoral College (312 to 226), and the Counties throughout America by 86%, and yet it is reported that I get 94% bad publicity. With such a Crooked and Corrupt Press, how did I win in such a LANDSLIDE? It is because the Media has NO credibility, and that is a very bad thing for our Nation! Why should I have to give “access” to such people? Perhaps Judge Kelly could explain that! In any event, I have an obligation to fight for the Success and Safety of our Country. FAKE NEWS IS A THREAT TO DEMOCRACY, and I will do whatever is necessary to make sure that the U.S.A. thrives."
The three organisations said their lawsuit was intended to defend their First Amendment rights and the principle that the government should not decide what the press reports.
"This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the outlets said in a joint statement.
The case has been assigned to US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first term. Kelly previously handled CNN reporter Jim Acosta's legal challenge after the White House revoked his press access in 2018.
CNN, MS NOW and Politico have asked the court to restore their access while the case proceeds. A hearing on their request is scheduled for Wednesday.
The dispute centres on whether the administration can restrict journalists' access to the White House based on objections to their reporting. The organisations have argued that their credentials were revoked without notice or a process to challenge the decision.
The launch of TRUMP TV adds a new element to the dispute, giving the administration a dedicated digital platform to distribute its own footage and announcements at a time when traditional White House television pool coverage has been disrupted.
The White House has described the platform as an "essentials station", featuring top videos, major remarks and highlights from the administration.

briefs.headline: Academicians write to Governor opposing the inter-university transfer of teachers
briefs.deck: The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Bill seeks to add one provision in Section 14A of the existing 2017 Act, which will allow inter-university transfer of both teaching and non-teaching employees as and when required, officials said
briefs.bodyText:
Several distinguished academics from the State and other parts of the country have expressed concern over the West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, saying academic productivity will be troubled seriously as the universities will no longer have any teaching, research and institutional autonomy.
The Bill was passed by the West Bengal Assembly on September 10.
In a letter to the Governor R.N. Ravi, who is also the Chancellor of all the universities, a group of 14 academicians said that every university is a distinct institution with its own academic structure, programmes and requirements, and that transferring faculty from one university to another could disturb the academic balance of both institutions.
"To move staff from one institution to another would impair the structural balance of both institutions and hamper their teaching and research programmes. Such programmes cannot be readily revised or interchanged," they stated.
They raised concerns over the ongoing research work across the universities. A university has specialized faculty who attract fresh researchers in that field. Laboratory and library facilities are developed to provide for those special areas. If those faculty members are transferred, young research students would be left without recourse. The material resources would lie unused or underused, they said.
They further pointed out that research funding for the major projects is often linked to the presence of expert faculty members serving as principal investigators. They said interdisciplinary and multi-institutional research projects could be “especially jeopardised” by faculty transfers.
Academics also argued that the development of newer universities should be undertaken through planned recruitment and adequate funding rather than sporadic transfers of teachers from established institutions.
"We are anxious that the new universities should be developed productively, but this cannot be done by sporadic transfer of faculty from elsewhere. At present, all or most of the new universities are grossly lacking in staff, infrastructure and facilities. Some of them have no full-time teachers at all. These needs must be met with due planning and sufficient funding, with extensive recruitment of permanent staff at all levels," the letter read.
They also urged the Governor urged to consider a fundamental issue of academic autonomy.
"All the universities would be brought under centralized administrative control. They could no longer develop freely, each according to its bent. Academic productivity would suffer seriously if university faculty felt they could no longer control their own affairs," they said.
The letter was written, among others, by Professor Emeritus of Jadavpur University Amita Chatterjee, former Palit Professor of Physics, Calcutta University Amitava Raychaudhuri, former IIM Calcutta Economics Professor Anup Sinha, Jadavpur University Raja Ramanna Professor Anupam Basu, former Rabindra Bharati University V.C. Sabya Sachi Basu Ray Choudhury, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research former Director Sabya Sachu Bhattacharya, former Director of Centre for Studies in Social Sciences, among others.
The West Bengal Universities and Colleges (Administration and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 was approved by the State Cabinet on September 8. It seeks to add one provision to Section 14A of the existing 2017 Act, which will allow inter-university transfer of both teaching and non-teaching employees as and when required, officials said.
The Bill was tabled by Higher Education Minister Jagannath Chattopadhyay during a special session of the State Assembly.
Addressing the assembly during the tabling of the Bill, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that through the proposed legislation, "so-called pundits" will be sent to newly established institutions that would benefit.

briefs.headline: 100% drought likely to be declared in Maharashtra by month-end, says Minister
briefs.deck: Never seen such severe dry spell: Cooperation Minister Babasaheb Patil; he adds govt. has initiated measures such as fee waiver for students, electricity bill waiver, and deployment of water tankers
briefs.bodyText:
Maharashtra Cooperation Minister Babasaheb Patil on Monday said the BJP-led Mahayuti government will soon declare 100% drought in the State. Speaking on the severity of the crisis, Mr. Patil said, “In my entire life, I have never seen such a severe drought. All crops, including soya bean, cotton and sugarcane, have suffered due to the dry spell and the loss is huge. The 100% drought declaration is expected by the end of September based on the National Disaster Response Fund norms.”
The Minister said the government has already initiated measures such as fee waiver for students, electricity bill waiver, and deployment of water tankers to provide relief.
The statement assumes significance as it is the first time a Minister has spoken of a 100% drought declaration. So far, the official position of the government has been that crop damage surveys and ground verification would be conducted after October 5.
Several regions in the State have been facing a prolonged dry spell, causing extensive crop loss and forcing farmers to incur heavy losses. According to the State Agriculture Department, rainfall has remained absent for over 20 days in at least 83 talukas across 20 districts. At least six districts, including Amravati, Solapur and Latur, have recorded rainfall deficit of 40-50%. Water tankers have started plying in villages such as Naichakur in Dharashiv district.
Advisory to districts
In view of the crisis, the State government has instructed district administrations to revive existing water sources and build water supply networks in villages facing shortage instead of treating tankers as the first solution.
A circular issued by the State Soil and Water Conservation Department on September 16 stated that the Groundwater Surveys and Development Agency will identify villages with drinking water shortage and submit the list to District Collectorates by October. District Collectors will have to plan interventions for the villages for the period between October and December. The plans are to be submitted by November 15, followed by plans for January-March 2027 by December 20, and for April-June 2027 by January 20, it stated.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Monday said the government would not wait for Central assistance to help farmers facing distress due to inadequate rainfall. “A formal crop loss assessment would be carried out after October 5 as required under the rules, following which the State would seek assistance from the Centre,” he told reporters.

stories.headline: Rain slows movement on several Bengaluru roads
stories.bodyText:
Light to moderate rains, which continued intermittently across parts of Bengaluru on Monday, slowed traffic on several roads during the evening peak hours, with waterlogging adding to the congestion in some areas.
Traffic was slow on stretches around Bagalur Cross, B. Narayanapura, Marathahalli-Kadubeesanahalli, and Manyata-Veerannapalya. At Bagalur Cross, waterlogging affected traffic movement towards both the city and the airport, while the Marathahalli-Kadubeesanahalli and Manyata-Veerannapalya stretches witnessed heavy congestion during peak hours, the Bengaluru traffic police said.
Traffic police and Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) officials said teams attended to complaints of waterlogging and took measures to clear the accumulated water and prevent prolonged stagnation.
GBA officials also carried out cleaning works at several waterlogging-prone locations, clearing garbage, plastic waste, and other debris that was obstructing the flow of rainwater into drains.
In the Shantinagar division, cleaning was carried out along M.G. Road and Chinnaswamy Stadium Road, while similar work was taken up at vulnerable locations in Gandhinagar, the GBA said. The rain also led to tree and branch falls at several locations across the city between 6 p.m. and 8.30 p.m.

stories.headline: Karnataka to track cancer patients after fake drug bust
stories.deck: In order to make it easy for laboratories, doctors, and pharmaceutical firms to differentiate between fake and original drugs, the department has written to the headquarters of Pfizer to release their reference standards, says Health Minister U.T. Khader
stories.bodyText:
Following the seizure of counterfeit drugs, especially those used to treat cancer, Health Department officials are now tracking patients to check the current status of their health.
Licences of 16 retail and wholesale pharmaceutical firms were cancelled and eight licenses were suspended.
Speaking to The Hindu, U.T. Khader, Minister for Health and Family Welfare, said, “Officials will track records of cancer patients from various private hospitals across the State. We will call them up and check the status of their health. They may have unknowingly bought these counterfeit drugs.”
“We don’t sell fake drugs at government hospitals, hence there is no question of tracking patients to know their status,” he added.
Mr. Khader stated that in order to make it easy for laboratories, doctors, and pharmaceutical firms to differentiate between fake and original drugs, the department has written to the headquarters of Pfizer to release their reference standards.
“When the fake drugs are sent to labs for testing, we need to have the company’s reference standards. It will make the process of drug testing easier for our department. However, the company hasn’t replied to our email so far. Hence, we have written to the Union government to take a note of the increasing number of fake drugs and medicines in the market, measures to identify them, and stop them from being sold in medical shops. State governments have a minor role to play in giving permissions to drug manufacturers and what is brought into the market for selling,” he said.
He added that the investigation of counterfeit drugs is ongoing, while the department is contemplating booking fake drug manufacturers, distributors, pharmaceutical firms, and medical store owners under Section 105 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), according to which if the act is done with the intent to cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death, the punishment is either life imprisonment or imprisonment for five to 10 years and penalty depending on the nature of offence.
An all-India health conclave will be hosted in Bengaluru in the third week of October, said Health Minister U.T. Khader. “Health Ministers from across all the States, FSDA officials from State governments, FSSAI officials and other stakeholders will be part of the conclave. We will not only discuss and debate but take some strong decisions to tackle issues like counterfeit drugs across the country,” he said.

stories.headline: Teachers oppose AI replacing third language in high schools in Karnataka
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Hundreds of teachers protested at Freedom Park Monday against state govt’s decision to introduce artificial intelligence (AI) as an alternative to the third language in some high schools of the state.
In a representation to govt, Deshiya Bhasha Hitarakshana Vedike said the move to introduce AI in school education was welcome, but making it a substitute for the third language would not be appropriate from the perspective of education or Karnataka’s multilingual tradition.
“Language and technology are both essential for students,” the forum said, urging the govt to introduce AI as a separate skill-based or elective subject without affecting third-language education.
The forum also raised concerns over govt’s July 14 draft notification on the recruitment to teaching posts in state-run high schools. It said the proposed recruitment of language teachers appeared to be restricted to Kannada and English, potentially affecting the teaching of other languages in govt schools.
According to the representation, Hindi, Sanskrit, Urdu, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Konkani, Tulu, Malayalam and Arabic have been taught in govt schools for several decades. 
Restricting the recruitment, it said, could affect students studying these languages as well as employment opportunities for qualified language teachers.
It sought three measures: recruitment of high-school teachers for all recognised languages, creation of separate language-teacher posts based on the number of students studying each language, and introduction of AI as a separate subject rather than as a replacement for the third language.
The forum said such measures would help preserve Karnataka’s multilingual education system while enabling students to acquire skills in emerging technologies.

briefs.headline: Higher passenger flow: Bengaluru airport to upgrade automated call enquiries
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: The Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) is all set to upgrade its on-premises Interactive Voice Response System (IVRS) with a focus on improving passenger experience, automation and its scalability.
IVRS systems involve an automated phone-in technology that lets callers get flight details and airport information by listening to pre-recorded voice menus and pressing phone keys or speaking commands.
KIA currently operates an IVRS system for passenger enquiries, flight information, lost-and-found routing and general enquiries using agents through the phone numbers 080-6678555 and 080-47406666. According to Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), the upgrade is being considered mainly because of the increasing passenger volumes, expansion of terminals and also to improve passenger engagement.
The new system is also likely to reduce the current workload of call agents. Currently, the airport has the capacity to handle a maximum of 400 inbound calls a day and 100 calls in the peak hour. BIAL anticipates a 50% traffic growth over the next five years, highlighting the need for sufficient scalability.
The upgraded smart IVRS system is expected to increase this capacity, helping BIAL handle at least 600 calls per day expected in the next five years and also increasing the peak-hour capacity to 150 calls.
The project will be carried out by an external partner who will initially conduct a detailed study about the requirements of the airport and will supply all the necessary systems.
Once the IVRS is upgraded, it will have the capability to resolve level 1 priority incidents within two hours. Critical incidents are expected to be solved in 15 minutes, while the least priority ones to be resolved within 48 hours.

briefs.headline: Karnataka high court stays deferment of revised minimum wages
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Karnataka high court has granted an interim stay on the operation of circulars issued by govt departments directing the withholding or deferment of revised minimum wages notified by the state on May 22, 2026.
Under the notification, minimum wages for 83 scheduled employments were revised based on skill levels, ranging from Rs 19,300 to Rs 31,100.
Justice HT Narendra Prasad passed the order while hearing petitions filed by the All India Trade Union Congress, Karnataka Rajya Sarkari Khayametharara Noukarara Okkuta, All India Central Council of Trade Unions and others.
According to the petitioners, the state govt had issued the May 22 notification under Sections 5(1)(a) and 5(1)(b) of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948. The revised wages were implemented and one month’s salary was paid to employees and workmen in accordance with the notification.
Thereafter, Karnataka state audit and accounts department issued a circular on July 29, 2026, while the directorate of municipal administration issued another on Aug 10, directing deferment of revised wages. The panchayat raj department also issued a similar circular.
The petitioners contended that the departments had no jurisdiction to defer implementation of a notification that continued to remain in force. They said salaries had not subsequently been paid in accordance with the May 22 notification and sought the high court’s intervention to protect the rights of workmen.
Considering the submissions, Justice Narendra Prasad stayed the operation of the impugned circulars until the next date of hearing. The court also ordered notice to the state government and the concerned departments.

briefs.headline: Shivamogga IS conspiracy case: Accused gets 6 years of rigorous imprisonment
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A special court for National Investigation Agency (NIA) cases has sentenced Huzair Farhan Baig to six years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) and imposed a fine of Rs 58,000, in connection with a terror conspiracy case involving the proscribed Islamic State (IS).
The case was initially registered by Shivamogga Rural police on Sept 19, 2022, and was subsequently taken over by NIA, which uncovered an IS module operating in Thirthahalli, Shivamogga.
According to NIA, the accused were allegedly mentored and guided online by a handler known as “Colonel”, later identified as Mohammed Shaheed Faisal, who is absconding in several terror cases being investigated by the agency. Faisal is accused of being involved in radicalising and recruiting youths to propagate the ideology of IS and further terrorist activities in India.
Huzair was radicalised and recruited by co-accused Maaz Muneer Ahmed and Syed Yasin. NIA said that on Maaz’s instructions, Huzair arranged a hideout in Bengaluru for terrorist activities.
Huzair received funds in cryptocurrency through accounts belonging to his friends. The cryptocurrency was subsequently converted into fiat currency and used to make payments towards the hideout. The funds were arranged by Maaz through the online handler.
NIA said it has so far filed four chargesheets against 12 accused persons in the case, with three accused already convicted and sentenced to six years of RI along with fines. The agency continues its efforts to trace Faisal, whom it has identified as the online handler.

briefs.headline: Karnataka HC orders court-monitored probe into KPSC irregularities; sets up SIT headed by DGP Alok Kumar
briefs.deck: While giving 100 days for the SIT to complete investigation and submit final report, the Court also directed it to submit an investigation progress report every 30 days
briefs.bodyText:
The Karnataka High Court on Monday ordered a court-monitored investigation — by constituting a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by senior IPS officer and Director-General of Police Alok Kumar — into the alleged large-scale irregularities in the recruitment processes conducted by the Karnataka State Public Service Commission (KPSC).
While giving 100 days for the SIT to complete the investigation and submit the final report, the court also directed it to submit an investigation progress report every 30 days.
Yatnal and others’ petition
Justice M. Nagaprasanna passed the order on petitions by Basanagouda R. Patil Yatnal, MLA, All Karnataka State Students’ Association, and Manjunath. The petitioners had sought a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into two cases: on selection of a daughter of the KPSC’s suspended chairperson Shivashankar S. Sahukar to the post of Industrial Extension Officer; and alleged illegalities in the process of selection of candidates to 400 posts of veterinary officers.
The court observed that, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the cases, it was not appropriate to permit the investigation to continue either with the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) or the jurisdictional police, but it was equally not convinced that entrusting the probe to the CBI was the only available course.
Meanwhile, the court has named IPS officers Divya V. Gopinath, Anoop A. Shetty, Kushal Choksey, and Kshama Mishra as other members of the SIT.
The court also directed the State government to issue a notification declaring this SIT to be a police station for the purposes of investigation.
Independent and impartial
“The SIT shall conduct the investigation independently, impartially and uninfluenced by any observation made in this order on the merits of the allegations,” the court said.
The court also made it clear that the investigation by the SIT shall not be confined by the persons presently named, the allegations presently made or the contours presently perceived. “If the evidence gathered during investigation reveals involvement of any other person, offence, transaction or act, having a nexus with the subject matter of investigation, the SIT shall follow the evidence wherever it leads, strictly in accordance with law,” the court said.
The court gave liberty to the SIT to use the services of forensic, cyber, financial, technical or other specialised assistance for an effective investigation.
The court said that the SIT should extend cooperation to the Enforcement Directorate (ED), which has re has taken up probe under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, and receive information from ED.
KPSC’s troubled history
Tracing the “troubled history” of KPSC recruitments since 1998, the court noted that history reveals allegations recurring with disquieting similarity such as nepotism, favouritism, fraud, corruption, tampering of OMR sheets and even allegations of answers being written for candidates elsewhere, while the examination was under way.
“History, it is said, should teach institutions. It cannot be permitted merely to repeat itself, recruitment after recruitment, at the cost of thousands of aspirants whose only capital is merit and whose only expectation is fairness,” the court observed.
Pointing out that thousands of young men and women spend the most productive years of their lives preparing for these examinations believing that merit will ultimately have its day, the court said that when a post is sold, an OMR sheet is tampered with, marks are manipulated or a selection is engineered, merit is not merely defeated; it is betrayed.”
Such betrayal, the court said, “breeds cynicism among the young and creates the dangerous perception that constitutional avenues themselves are available for purchase. A recruitment scam in a Public Service Commission in particular is not merely a theft of post; it is a theft of equality of opportunity.”

stories.headline: Starbucks to set up GCC in Chennai

stories.headline: GST rate rejig helps consumers upgrade
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: A year after 
GST rates
 were cut, automobile dispatches have continued to climb. Several two-wheeler users moved to four-wheelers as price cuts improved affordability, TV buyers have shifted towards larger sets and consumer goods volumes picked up in the Oct-Dec quarter, although they are now under pressure due to the West Asia crisis.
Passenger vehicle dispatches reached a record 12.7 lakh units in April–June 2026, up 25.9% from a year earlier, according to Siam. Two-wheeler dispatches rose 20.3% to 56.3 lakh units. Siam has cited lower GST rates and easier financing among the factors supporting demand. Its figures measure supplies to dealers, rather than purchases by customers.
Television shipments tell a different story. India’s smart TV shipments grew 10% year-on-year in Oct–Dec 2025, according to Counterpoint Research, before falling 3% in Jan-March 2026. TVs sized 55 inches and above were the fastest-growing category in the March quarter, accounting for nearly one-third of shipments.
The trend, however, got stalled because of the uncertainty triggered by Operation Epic Fury US and Israel launched against Iran on Feb 28 and Counterpoint’s TV tracker recorded a 9.8% decline in shipments in April–June. GST on TVs above 32 inches, including 55-inch models, was slashed from 28% to 18% last Sept.
Keshav Bansal, director at Intex Technologies, said the cut created “a meaningful affordability window” for bigger TVs. Intex’s consumer durables business grew 80% in FY26, with smart TVs among the drivers, he said. But “unit volumes have not risen in proportion to value growth; the more significant shift has been in product mix,” as buyers chose larger screens and better technology.
Bansal said lower GST also supported air-conditioner demand, alongside a favourable summer and a lower comparison base. Rising input costs, including memory chips for TVs, and the cost of meeting newer energy-efficiency norms for ACs have since absorbed part of the tax benefit, he said.
“In the long-term, it is definitely a positive, especially with people looking to move to branded products. But there is some impact in the short run due to the recent increase in input prices. Also, full refund of input tax credit will help in offsetting some of the cost,” said Liberty Shoes executive director Anupam Bansal.
FMCG companies initially saw an improvement in demand after the rate changes. Volume growth picked up at companies, including Hindustan Unilever, Marico and Dabur. Nestlé India reported its strongest volume growth in five years in the Dec 2025 quarter, attributing it partly to a market recovery supported by GST benefits.
That early lift has come under pressure as companies raised prices to offset higher costs. Companies and analysts are keeping a close watch on sales in the current quarter.

stories.headline: Hikal incubates animal health, personal care businesses for growth
stories.deck: ‘We realised that, using the same principles and some of the same assets, we could enter a different line of business without much investment,’ said Anish Swadi, Senior President, Business Transformation
stories.bodyText:
Hikal Ltd., the active ingredients & intermediates company, has recast its growth strategy around diversification, capital efficiency and higher-value chemistry, choosing adjacent businesses that can use its manufacturing assets, regulatory systems and multinational customer relationships.
During COVID-19, the next generation of leadership, led by Sameer Hiremath, Vice-Chairman and Managing Director and Anish Swadi, Senior President, Business Transformation, examined how far pharmaceuticals and crop protection, which are the core business, could grow, their capital needs and likely returns.
As per the advice of consultants, the company came out with a 2030 strategy, aimed at creating value over six to seven years rather than pursuing turnover alone.
Animal health and personal care were selected because they were close to Hikal’s capabilities and customers, while providing diversification without requiring an entirely new manufacturing platform.
“We realised that, using the same principles and some of the same assets, we could enter a different line of business without much investment. From a diversification perspective, that was very good for the business,” said Mr. Swadi.
Hikal could apply its pharmaceutical processes to animal-health ingredients. In personal care, it could approach different divisions of multinational companies for which it was already an approved supplier.
The approach is designed to reduce exposure to market cycles. Crop protection faced prolonged destocking and pricing pressure after COVID-19, while pharmaceutical operations were affected by regulatory remediation. So Hikal decided to incubate the new businesses during the downturn, the top executives said.
“Today, 60% of the revenue comes from pharma and around 40 % from crop protection. Over the next three to four years this will change significantly” Mr. Hiremath said.
The company aims to increase revenue from Animal Health to more than ₹400 crore by FY30 where margins would be in double digits once operating leverage is achieved.
Personal care division began commercial production recently at Panoli and is expected to cross ₹200 crore in revenue by FY30.
For FY26, Hikal reported revenue of ₹1,713 crore and EBITDA of ₹232.8 crore, translating into a 13.6% margin. A revenue growth of 14 - 16% is expected in FY27.
“We do not need to raise significant debt unless we undertake a major acquisition, which is currently not in the cards. Under the current plan, we have healthy cash flows and strong financials,” Mr. Hiremath said.
Rather than making acquisitions merely to add turnover, Hikal will prioritise technology partnerships and selective investments that strengthen existing chemistry platforms and produce returns sooner, he stated.

briefs.headline: MS expands India capacity for cloud and AI services
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Microsoft's new India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad is among its largest infrastructure investments in Asia, the company's India and South Asia president Puneet Chandok said, as it expands capacity for cloud and AI services.
The facility is part of Microsoft's $20.5 billion investment commitment across Asia. Chandok did not disclose how much of that would be spent on which particular business interests. He said the expansion must account for the resources data centres consume and what surrounding communities gain. "How do you learn to build a data centre? It's by making sure that you're net accretive to the community," he told TOI, citing water, power and jobs.
Chandok said advanced air cooling would eliminate water use for cooling at the new facilities. He also said Microsoft was replenishing water near its data centres and had committed to one gigawatt of green energy, of which 60 megawatts was already flowing. The company has not disclosed the new region's total power demand, making it difficult to assess those commitments against its expected resource use.
Microsoft is pairing the infrastructure push with AI training, Chandok said. 
He put the number of people trained at 10 million and said close to 125,000 had secured jobs. The company also has more than 17,000 engineers across 10 Indian cities, he said.
Speaking at the launch, MeitY secretary S Krishnan urged Microsoft to expand its development and research operations in India alongside its data centres. He said global investment in AI infrastructure should help build domestic capabilities in areas including AI servers and semiconductors, while creating higher-quality jobs. Krishnan argued that future data centres should be located closer to electricity-generation centres, rather than concentrated around connectivity hubs.

briefs.headline: Small-city ecomm surges, order values trail big markets
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Online shopping is expanding beyond India's biggest cities, but the value of those purchases remains concentrated in larger markets.
Of more than 200 million orders processed in the last 12 months up to July this year, 57.2% originated outside the 96 largest cities, but these orders accounted for only 39.3% of total transaction value. Their average order value was Rs 830, less than half the Rs 1,714 recorded in the largest cities.
EasyEcom, an ecommerce software company, compiled the data from transactions processed through marketplaces, brand websites, quick-comm platforms, distributors and other channels connected to its system. Its customers include Borosil, Cred, Minimalist and Pilgrim, among others.
The gap suggests that ecommerce growth outside the biggest cities is driven more by higher transaction volumes than by higher-value purchases. This could have implications for brands deciding where to hold inventory and how to manage deliveries across a wider network.
The divide is even sharper at the state level. Of the 15 largest states in the dataset, 13 changed position when ranked by transaction value rather than order volume. Haryana moved from 11th by orders to third by value, supported by higher-value transactions in Gurugram and Sonipat. Its average order value of Rs 3,804 was more than six times Bihar's Rs 609. 
Bihar moved in the opposite direction, falling from 10th by volume to 15th by value.
At the city level, Bengaluru was the largest market by order count, with around 11 million orders, 84% more than Mumbai. Gurugram ranked only seventh by volume but second by value, at Rs 1,848 crore. Its average order value of Rs 6,693 was more than four times Delhi's Rs 1,499.

briefs.headline: Govt winds up telecom commission
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Govt has with immediate effect dissolved its apex decision-making body for telecom and digital communication - digital communications commission (DCC), which was originally established as telecom commission in 1989, before being renamed in 2018. The communication ministry's department of telecommunication (DoT) notified this decision through a Sept 19, 2026 resolution that was published in the Gazette of India. "With effect from date of publication of this resolution, the DCC shall stand dissolved," says the gazette.
Decisions for projects up to Rs 100 crore can be taken by the secretary DoT, up to Rs 500 crore by the telecom minister and those above Rs 500 crore to Rs 1,000 crore were considered by the DCC. Now the same will be referred to the expenditure finance committee.
